issues.title: Account takeover through the legacy employee API
issues.text: PUT /api/employees/:id applied the whole request body, so a vendor could point their employee at any user (even an admin) and the handler then rewrote that user's login email. A password reset finished the takeover. The same hole let a vendor move an employee onto another vendor and read its attendees. Updates now use an allowlist and never touch the login email.

issues.title: One payment could confirm many orders and registrations
issues.text: Booking confirm only checked the amount, and registration confirm checked nothing, so one succeeded Stripe payment could be replayed to confirm other pending orders of the same price, or any number of paid registrations. Both now require the payment to be the one created for that record.

issues.title: Competition entries marked paid with someone else's payment
issues.text: Finalizing an AI Art Competition entry only checked that the Stripe session was paid, so one paid session could finalize unlimited free drafts. It must now be the session created for that entry.

issues.title: Late Stripe events could revive refunded orders
issues.text: With Stripe now retrying failed webhooks, a delayed "payment succeeded" could flip a refunded order back to paid, re-send confirmation emails and count the affiliate sale twice. Each is now guarded.

issues.title: Public review link created accounts, fake bookings and certificates
issues.text: Anyone who knew an event id could create verified accounts, paid-looking registrations, reviews and certificates for any email, and learn account ids. The shared link now carries a secret token, never acts as an existing account unless that user logs in, and is rate limited. Offline attendees keep working; links shared before this change must be regenerated.

issues.title: Ticket transfer brought used and refunded tickets back
issues.text: Transferring a ticket reset it to active with a fresh QR code, so a checked-in, cancelled or refunded ticket became valid again. Only active, unused tickets can be transferred now.

issues.title: Any vendor could read or issue tickets for other vendors' events
issues.text: Any vendor could list the tickets (attendee names and emails) of any order, and mint valid tickets for another vendor's event. Both are now limited to the event's own vendor and staff.

issues.title: Vendors could issue certificates under other vendors' events
issues.text: Single and bulk certificate generation didn't check event ownership, so a vendor could issue official certificates under a competitor's event to any email.

issues.title: Student signup could plant children on other accounts
issues.text: The public student-program form attached a child to any existing account by email and put the submitted text into the welcome email as raw HTML (phishing from our domain). Existing accounts now need their owner logged in, the email is escaped, the temporary password is cryptographically random, and the form is rate limited.

issues.title: Scripts inside uploaded SVG images ran on the API domain
issues.text: Uploaded files are served from the API origin, so a script inside an uploaded SVG ran there when the file was opened directly. SVG/XML/HTML now get a sandboxing CSP (images and PDFs still display), and customer booking attachments no longer accept SVG.

issues.title: Certificate lookup exposed children's names to anyone
issues.text: Typing any email on the public certificate lookup showed the recipients' names, events and PDF links. Now only the logged-in owner sees the list; anyone else gets "check your inbox" and the list is emailed to that address.

issues.title: Vendors could give themselves paid promotion and ratings
issues.text: Creating an event accepted isFeatured, premium promotion, featuredUntil and fake rating counts from the request. One shared protected-field list now covers create and update.

issues.title: Search boxes accepted regular expressions
issues.text: 76 search sites put raw text into database regex queries: typing "(" returned a 500, and crafted patterns could tie up the database. Searches now match the literal text.

issues.title: Public forms could be used to spam inboxes
issues.text: Contact, newsletter, partnership, lead and competition-draft forms only had the general rate limit. Each now allows 60 submissions an hour per network, and the event lead form validates its fields (a malformed name used to cause a 500).

issues.title: Anyone could burn the paid exchange-rate quota
issues.text: POST /api/currency/refresh was public and called the paid FX API every time. It is now admin-only; nothing in the site used it.

issues.title: Users could be signed out everywhere after a quick refresh
issues.text: Two refresh tokens issued in the same second were identical, so an early refresh looked like token theft and signed the user out on every device. Each token is now unique.

issues.title: Vendor analytics page never loaded
issues.text: A public route declared earlier caught /events/vendor/analytics, so vendors always got "Invalid event ID". Found by the new route-auth check.

issues.title: Affiliates were never credited for paid orders
issues.text: The payment webhook looked affiliates up by the wrong field name, so no paid order ever recorded an affiliate conversion. Past orders with an affiliate code may need a backfill.

issues.title: Transferring a ticket to a new email always failed
issues.text: It tried to create an account without a password and returned a 500. It now asks the recipient to sign up first.

issues.title: Paid competition entries lost when the tab was closed
issues.text: Only the browser's return trip finalized an entry, so a parent who paid and closed the tab kept an unpaid draft and no confirmation. The Stripe webhook now finalizes it too, exactly once.

issues.title: Events created through one route didn't belong to their vendor
issues.text: POST /api/events stored the vendor's user id instead of the vendor id, so later ownership checks treated the vendor as a stranger. New events store the vendor id; older ones keep working until migrateEventVendorIds runs.

issues.title: Teachers got an error opening their own bookings
issues.text: Bookings pointed at a "TeachingEvent" model that doesn't exist, so reading a booking always returned a 500.

issues.title: Stale Stripe events could mislead customers or downgrade vendors
issues.text: A late "payment failed" event notified customers who had already paid, and an out-of-order subscription event could downgrade a paying vendor. Subscription and invoice errors were also swallowed, losing the update. Now: no notice for paid orders, the subscription's current state is read from Stripe, and failures make Stripe retry.

issues.title: Seeded test data broke every vendor check
issues.text: The local seed never created vendor profiles, so seeded events and employees pointed at nothing and vendor features couldn't be tested locally. Seeded vendors now get verified profiles.

issues.title: CI never ran the browser tests or enforced coverage and audits
issues.text: Playwright tests existed but never ran in CI, coverage thresholds were never checked, and npm audit couldn't fail. Every PR now runs the browser tests against a real seeded backend, a ZAP security scan, CodeQL, a blocking dependency audit (reviewed exceptions only) and a coverage gate. scripts/verify.sh runs the same checks locally.

issues.title: Nothing caught a route that forgot its login check
issues.text: Tests now mount the real route table and call every API route without login (and every admin route as a customer). Any route that isn't on the reviewed public list must refuse, so a new public route fails CI until reviewed.

issues.title: Payment and booking code paths couldn't be tested
issues.text: The test database couldn't run transactions, which 27 code paths use. Tests now run on a replica set like production.

issues.title: Old /book/<id> links went to a broken page
issues.text: The redirect sent visitors to the literal path /booking/:eventId. It now uses the real event id.

issues.title: An admin endpoint returned the new user's password hash
issues.text: Creating a vendor from a partnership returned the full user document, password hash included. User documents now never serialize password or OTP hashes, on any endpoint. The public partner directory also stopped returning phone numbers, payment session ids and attachments.

issues.title: Employees could check tickets in as a colleague
issues.text: The check-in API trusted the employee id in the request, any venue assignment authorised every event, and vendors could read every vendor's check-in logs. Check-ins are now tied to the logged-in employee and their assigned events, and logs are limited to the vendor's own events.

issues.title: Affiliates could set their own earnings
issues.text: Applying or editing an affiliate profile accepted any field, including commission earned and totals. Only the form's fields are accepted now. Applying had also always failed, because the affiliate code was generated after validation.

issues.title: Vendors could approve their own venues
issues.text: Venue updates accepted isApproved and promotion fields. Creating a venue also always failed (venue-type mismatch and missing required fields); both are fixed.

issues.title: Anyone could read unmoderated blog comments
issues.text: The public comment list accepted ?status=pending. It now returns published comments only, and deleting a comment twice no longer pushes the count below zero.

issues.title: Anyone could rewrite a newsletter subscriber's details
issues.text: Subscribing with an existing email overwrote that subscriber's name, city and preferences. Existing subscribers are left as they are, and the welcome email escapes the name.

issues.title: Event cards reloaded the whole site, sometimes on another domain
issues.text: Cards linked to an absolute URL built from the configured site address, so every click was a full reload to that host. They now navigate inside the app.

issues.title: Frontend type-check had 38 errors
issues.text: All were unused code (including the never-shown old competition payment step). The type-check is clean, so the CI frontend job can pass.

issues.title: Admin review moderation did nothing
issues.text: The moderation queue and the dashboard activity feed crashed once any review existed, and approve, reject and flag were empty stubs. They now work and share one code path with the main review moderation (approving issues the certificate).

issues.title: Bad input crashed with a server error
issues.text: A malformed id anywhere returned 500, and production 500s echoed internal database messages. Malformed input now gets a 400 with a plain message, internals stay in the log, and the teacher profile page no longer crashes.

issues.title: Venue click tracking never recorded anything
issues.text: Anonymous clicks on external-booking venues hit a login check first and returned 401. The public tracking routes now come before it.

issues.title: Categories couldn't be created without a slug
issues.text: The slug was generated after validation had already rejected it. It's now generated first.

issues.title: Blog and reel likes could be inflated
issues.text: Blog likes trusted a spoofable IP header, and reel likes had no limit at all (and could go negative). Each client can now like once.

issues.title: Settings and banners crashed on bad values
issues.text: A mistyped settings value or an unknown image id returned 500; both now return a clear 4xx.

issues.title: Most controllers had no tests
issues.text: Added 260 controller tests (registration, check-in, affiliates, venues, blogs, partnerships, moderation and more) plus 96 ownership and auth tests. They found the 44 bugs fixed in this pass.

issues.title: Admin refunds never refunded the card
issues.text: The admin refund and bulk refund buttons marked the order refunded, but never asked Stripe to return the money. All admin refund endpoints now refund through Stripe, and a retry can't refund twice.

issues.title: Refunded orders were still paid out to vendors
issues.text: A refund left the order's revenue in the vendor payout pool and its tickets still scannable. A full refund, whether made here or in the Stripe dashboard, now voids the tickets and takes the revenue out of payouts.

issues.title: One competition payment could unlock any number of entries
issues.text: Confirming a National Day entry checked that a Stripe payment was complete, but not which entry it paid for, so one paid checkout link could be reused to mark other unpaid entries as paid. The payment now has to belong to the entry being confirmed.

issues.title: Page-view beacon had no rate limit or field checks
issues.text: POST /api/track/pageview wrote whatever it was sent, as fast as it was sent, and hashed IPs without a salt. It now has a rate limiter, type and length checks on every field, and a salted IP hash (set ANALYTICS_IP_SALT).

issues.title: Traffic numbers couldn't say where visitors came from
issues.text: Page views now carry an anonymous visitor id, the traffic source (UTM tags or referrer), browser, OS and visible time; new accounts keep the source they first arrived from. Search, filter, Book click, favourite, share, blog view, organiser profile click, sign-up and login events are tracked. A nightly rollup keeps daily and monthly totals after the 90-day raw data expires, and seven admin-only reports read them.

issues.title: Two trackers counted the same visit as two sessions
issues.text: Page views and event clicks each kept their own session id, so they couldn't be joined into a funnel. One tracker now sends a shared session id and an anonymous visitor id, captures the landing UTM tags and referrer, and stops entirely when the browser has Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track on. The admin Traffic page gets seven report tabs with CSV export.

issues.title: Highlights report didn't show where visitors come from
issues.text: The Platform Highlights PDF now has a 'Where visitors come from' chart (search engines, social media, WhatsApp, email, ads, other websites, direct), counted per visitor. It only appears once page views with a known source exist.

issues.title: Anyone with a National Day reference could read or replace the entry
issues.text: References are nearly sequential, and lookup and artwork upload needed only the reference, so a stranger could read a child's details and overwrite their artwork. Both now need the parent email too, and a wrong email looks the same as a missing entry. Lookups also no longer miss entries older than the newest 100.

issues.title: Paying for a National Day entry could attach a child to someone else's account
issues.text: Finalize looked up the parent account by the email typed on the form and added the child to it, so anyone could add children to an existing account. Children are now only added to an account that finalize itself just created.

issues.title: Competition payment could be skipped, and the school price chosen freely
issues.text: Sending session_id=TEST_PAYMENT_SKIP finalized National Day and AI Art entries without paying in any non-production setup, and anyone could choose the AED 40 school bulk price. The skip now needs ALLOW_TEST_PAYMENT_SKIP=true, and the school price needs a code listed in NATIONAL_DAY_SCHOOL_CODES.

issues.title: National Day artwork public, email HTML injection, leaked test credentials
issues.text: Artwork downloads are now admin-only, names in emails are HTML-escaped, the admin search escapes regex input, temp passwords use a secure random generator, and the hard-coded Ethereal mailbox login was removed (it is still in git history, so treat that mailbox as public).

issues.title: A coupon's last use could be taken twice, and unpaid orders burnt uses
issues.text: Coupon limits were checked and counted in separate steps, so two checkouts at once could both use the last allowed use. Uses also stayed spent when an unpaid order was cancelled, failed payment or expired. The check and the count now happen in one database update, and those orders give the use back.

issues.title: Refund tests flaky under the full suite
issues.text: Refund transactions sometimes aborted while other test files were still building indexes. Refunds now retry transient transaction errors with a short backoff and the refund tests build their indexes first. They pass on their own every time but can still fail when the whole suite runs at once; see the known failures note.

issues.title: Missing events return 404 and drafts explain themselves
issues.text: Event lookups that found nothing returned 500 and unpublished events leaked a generic error. They now return a proper 404 and a clear draft message (N25, N27).

issues.title: Delete guards for vendors, teachers and admin events
issues.text: Permanent delete is blocked when the record still has bookings or live events (N26).

issues.title: Teacher/vendor import and ticket generation fixes
issues.text: Imported bookings now carry source, payment method and phone; ticket generate works; temp passwords come from one helper; vendor-scoped queries use the vendor profile id (N03, N04, N05, N08, N21).

issues.title: Employee API is self-service only
issues.text: Legacy /api/employees management routes are removed; assigned events and my-reports added; dead fallbacks removed (N01, N02, N06).

issues.title: Analytics beacons no longer 403
issues.text: Tracking beacons are exempt from CSRF, and the CSRF token is stored before post-login tracking fires (N10, N11).

issues.title: Self-service data export and account deletion
issues.text: New endpoints let users download their data and anonymise their account; the fake 2FA toggle is gone (N09).

issues.title: Accessibility and contrast pass
issues.text: Daily theme colours meet WCAG AA, carousel dots have touch targets and focus rings, heading levels fixed, popups suppressed on task-critical pages, invalid Tailwind tokens fixed, 16 dead API helpers removed.

issues.title: npm audit fixes
issues.text: Backend and frontend dependencies updated for known advisories (N23, N24).

issues.title: No high-severity advisories left in production dependencies
issues.text: Backend puppeteer moved to 25 (certificate and report PDFs still pass their tests). Frontend pins @grpc/grpc-js to 1.14 through an npm override, which clears the firebase advisories without the downgrade npm audit fix --force would have done.

issues.title: Frontend unit tests run again
issues.text: Jest now loads the Vite code (import.meta rewrite, path aliases, uuid stub) and the TipTap tests pass. Five old suites that mocked fetch against removed Redux slices were deleted. 22 frontend tests pass.

issues.title: Young Voices and Reel entries could be marked paid with someone else's payment
issues.text: Finalizing a GCC or Reel entry only checked that the Stripe session was paid, so one paid session could finalize any number of other drafts. The session must now be the one created for that entry, at the entry fee. The paid flag is also claimed with a single conditional update, so a double click or retry no longer repeats the account, order and email work. The TEST_PAYMENT_SKIP bypass now needs ALLOW_TEST_PAYMENT_SKIP=true, like the older competitions.

issues.title: Entry details and uploads open to anyone holding a reference number
issues.text: Looking up a Young Voices or Reel entry only checked the parent email when one was supplied, so leaving it out returned the child's name, school and the parent's name and email. Story and reel uploads checked nothing, so anyone could overwrite another family's entry. Both now require the parent email; a wrong email and an unknown reference return the same 404; a Reel under review can no longer be overwritten. Confirmation emails carry the email in the link so the normal flow is unchanged.

issues.title: Story manuscripts could be downloaded without logging in
issues.text: The manuscript download link had no login or role check. It is now admin-only. Anything that is not a PDF is always served as a download with nosniff and a sandbox policy, and story uploads accept only PDF or Word, reel uploads only video.

issues.title: Winter Camp registration could give a free order for a paid event
issues.text: The public form sent event ids or titles and every match got a confirmed AED 0 order and a seat taken, paid events included. It can now only match live events that are actually free; anything else falls back to the plain registration order. Non-text values are rejected and the lists are capped.

issues.title: Weak temporary passwords and unescaped email text in the new competitions
issues.text: Parent accounts created by Young Voices, Reel and Winter Camp used Math.random for the temporary password; they now use the same secure generator as the other competitions. Names, emails, grade, city and programs are HTML-escaped in the welcome and confirmation emails, and the new public forms have the same hourly rate limit as the other public forms.

issues.title: Mailchimp server prefix could send the API key to another host
issues.text: The prefix from the admin settings goes into the Mailchimp hostname, so a value like evil.com/# would have sent the API key there. The prefix (for example us21) and the audience id are now strictly validated when saved and again before every use.

issues.title: Marketing sync only for people who explicitly opted in
issues.text: The account setting for marketing email is on for everyone by default, so it is not consent. Registered users are now synced to Sender or Mailchimp only after an unticked sign-up checkbox (or later opt-in) and a verified email. Newsletter subscribers keep syncing. Unsubscribes, including ones made inside the provider, are always honoured.

issues.title: Merge kept the hardened competition payments and records one order per payment
issues.text: Merging the aditya branch kept the session-ownership check and the shared, run-once finalize for AI Art and National Day. The new order record for competition payments (admin revenue) now lives in that shared step, so the browser finalize and the Stripe webhook cannot record it twice.

tests.title: Review link token
steps: As admin, open an event in Admin → Events → Edit and click Generate Review Link; the link ends with ?t=…
Open the link without the ?t= part.
Open the full link and enter a new email, then submit a rating.
Open it again with customer@gema.com while logged out.
tests.expect: Without the token the page says the link is invalid. A new email can review. An existing account is asked to log in first.

tests.title: Certificate lookup
steps: Logged out, open /certificates/lookup and enter an email that has a certificate.
Open Mailpit at http://localhost:8025.
Log in as that user and open the page again.
tests.expect: Logged out: "Check your inbox" and nothing listed; the list arrives by email. Logged in: the list shows on the page.

tests.title: Student program signup
steps: Logged out, open /student-program and submit the form with customer@gema.com.
Submit again with a brand-new email.
tests.expect: The first is refused with "already has a Kidrove account, please log in". The second succeeds and the welcome email arrives in Mailpit.

tests.title: Search with special characters
steps: Search the blog for ( and for C++.
Search venues for [a-z.
tests.expect: Results load normally (empty or matching); no error page.

tests.title: Uploaded SVG can't run scripts
steps: As a vendor, upload an SVG containing <script>alert(1)</script> as an event image.
Open the image URL directly in a new tab.
tests.expect: The image shows (or is blank) and no alert appears. The response has a Content-Security-Policy with sandbox.

tests.title: Vendor analytics
steps: Log in as vendor@gema.com and open the analytics section of the vendor dashboard.
tests.expect: The analytics load; no "Invalid event ID" error.

tests.title: Competition entry survives a closed tab
steps: Open /ai-art-competition, fill the form and pay with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242.
On Stripe's success screen, close the tab before it redirects back.
As admin, open the competition submissions list.
tests.expect: The entry shows as paid, and exactly one confirmation email is in Mailpit.

tests.title: Full pre-deploy check
steps: From the repo root, with Docker running: ./scripts/verify.sh
Open the report: cd frontend && npx playwright show-report
tests.expect: It ends with "All checks passed". Any failure stops it with the failing step named.

tests.title: Admin refund returns the money
steps: Book an event as a customer and pay with 4242 4242 4242 4242.
As admin, open the order and click Refund.
Check the payment in the Stripe test dashboard, and the customer's ticket.
tests.expect: Stripe shows the payment refunded; the ticket shows as refunded and no longer checks in.

tests.title: National Day payment can't be reused
steps: Register two National Day entries; pay for the first with 4242 4242 4242 4242 and note the session_id in the success URL.
Call POST finalize for the second entry's submissionId with the first entry's session_id.
tests.expect: The request fails with "Payment does not match this submission." and the second entry stays unpaid.

tests.title: Daily rollup and backfill
steps: Browse a few pages, then in the backend run: npx ts-node -e "require('./src/config/database').connectDB().then(()=>require('./src/services/analyticsRollup.service').runNightlyRollup()).then(()=>process.exit())"
In Mongo, look at the analyticsdailies collection.
tests.expect: One period:"day" row per day of the last 90 days and a period:"month" row for this month; today's row counts the pages you just browsed. Running it again changes nothing.

tests.title: Analytics smoke test: attribution and actions
steps: Open http://localhost:5173/?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=test.
Search for an activity, apply an age and a city filter, open an event, click Book, share the event and a blog.
Register a new account in the same window.
As admin, open Traffic: check Overview, Marketing (Social media row, 'test' campaign), Conversions, Behaviour (your search and filters), Events, Content & SEO, Organisers. Export a CSV from one tab.
In Mongo, find the new user and look at its acquisition field.
tests.expect: Each tab shows your visit and actions; acquisition.channel is "social" and utmCampaign "test". The CSV opens with the same rows.

tests.title: Analytics: returning visitors and privacy signals
steps: In a normal window, open the site, close the tab, open it again and browse.
Turn on Global Privacy Control (Brave, or Firefox privacy.globalprivacycontrol.enabled) or Do Not Track, reload, and watch DevTools Network.
Open the admin Traffic page on a phone-width window.
tests.expect: The second visit counts as returning (Overview new/returning). With GPC or DNT on there are no requests to /track/pageview, /track/engagement or /analytics/track. The tabs scroll sideways instead of overflowing the page.

tests.title: Highlights PDF shows visitor sources
tests.where: Local (Docker), after the smoke test above
steps: As admin, open Analytics and download the Platform Highlights report for the last 30 days.
tests.expect: The Platform Engagement card has a 'Where visitors come from' chart that includes Social media.

tests.title: National Day entry needs the parent email
steps: Register a National Day entry and note the reference (UAE2026-xxxxxxxx).
Open /national-day-art-competition/submit?ref=<reference> and look up with a different email, then with the parent email.
tests.expect: A different email says no registration was found; the parent email shows the entry. The link in the confirmation email fills in both.

tests.title: Coupon last use and cancelled orders
steps: As admin, create a coupon with a total usage limit of 1.
As a customer, start a booking, apply the coupon, then cancel the unpaid order.
Start another booking and apply the same coupon.
tests.expect: The second booking accepts the coupon (the cancelled order gave its use back). After paying, a third attempt says the coupon has reached its usage limit.

tests.title: Account data export and deletion
steps: Log in as a customer and open Profile.
Click Download my data, then Delete account and confirm.
tests.expect: A JSON export downloads; after deletion the account is anonymised and you can no longer log in.

tests.title: Young Voices and Reel entries need the parent email
steps: Register a Young Voices entry and pay with the Stripe test card.
Open the submit link from the confirmation email (it ends in ?ref=...&email=...): the entry loads.
Remove &email=... from the address: the page asks for the parent email instead of loading.
Enter a different email, then the right one.
tests.expect: A wrong email says no registration was found (the same message as an unknown reference); the right email loads the entry. Repeat for the Reel Challenge.

tests.title: Winter Camp cannot be used to get a paid event for free
steps: Have one free and one paid workshop live, and note the paid one's remaining seats.
Submit the Winter Camp form choosing both.
Open Admin > Orders and the paid workshop.
tests.expect: The AED 0 order lists only the free workshop and only its seat count drops; the paid workshop is untouched.

tests.title: Email marketing provider settings
steps: Open Admin > Settings > Email Marketing, choose Mailchimp, enter an API key, audience id and prefix us21, then Save.
Reload the page and look at the key field.
Enter the prefix evil.com and Save.
Switch back to Development and send a test email from Admin > Email Marketing > Compose.
tests.expect: The key is never shown again (only 'saved here'); the bad prefix is rejected; the test email appears in Mailpit at http://localhost:8025.

tests.title: Registered users sync to the marketing provider only after opting in
steps: Register one account leaving the marketing checkbox unticked and another with it ticked, and verify both emails.
Open the Email Marketing overview and look at the contact sync counts.
tests.expect: Only the ticked account produces a contact sync; the unticked one produces none.
